chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, who said: Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Aḥmasī narrated to me, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said:

I entered upon ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), and I was kept waiting in the courtyard for a while. Then I entered the house, and he was picking up something, and he put his hand from behind the curtain, then handed it to whoever was in the house. So I said: May I be sacrificed for you, what is this thing that I see you picking up?
He said: It is a remnant from the fluff of the angels. We gather it when we are alone and make it as a plaything for our children.
So I said: May I be sacrificed for you, do they indeed come to you? He said: O Abū Ḥamzah, they indeed crowd upon our cushions.

key_terms.أَوْلَادِنَا: our children, referring to the Imam's family
key_terms.السِّتْرِ: the curtain or screen behind which the Imam reached his hand
key_terms.زَغَبِ الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the soft fluff or down of the angels mentioned as a remnant gathered by the Imam
key_terms.سَيْحًا: a plaything or something used for the amusement of children in this context
key_terms.فَضْلَةٌ: a leftover remnant or trace of something

ai.seo_question: Do angels visit the Imams and leave traces in their gatherings?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī visiting Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) and witnessing a trace left by the angels. The narration presents the nearness of the angels to the Imam and indicates a special rank of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), to the extent that angels gather around them intimately.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam who said, ‘Malik Bin Atiyya Al Ahmasy narrated to me, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said,

‘I went over to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bn Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and I was withheld in the room for a while. Then I entered the room and he<sup>asws</sup> was picking up something and he<sup>asws</sup> inserted his<sup>asws</sup> hand from behind the curtain, and the one who was in the room took it’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! This which I saw you<sup>asws</sup> pick up, which things was it?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Remnant from the fluff of the Angels. We<sup>asws</sup> gather it when they are around us<sup>asws</sup> to make it to amuse our<sup>asws</sup> children’.

So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And they (Angels) tend to come to you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Hamza! They tend to crowd upon our<sup>asws</sup> cushions’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam who hassaaid that Malik ibn ‘Atiyya al-Ahmasi narrated to him from abu Hamza al-Thumali who has said the following.

“Once I went to see Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) and I became confounded in the room for an hour then I went inside the house while he was picking up things and would give to someone behind the curtain. I then said, may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, What was that thing that I saw you picking up?”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “The fuzz from the angels when they come to meet us and we use it amuse our children.”
I then said, may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, do they they come to you?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “O abu Hamza, they become crowded over our furnishings.”
